name: phase4-constraint-handling
description: Phase 4 experiment: four constraint-handling strategies on the same optimizer (DE/rand/1/bin@1, literature defaults), the same problems and the same seeds (RF-4.10). Scenarios, budgets, seeds, coefficients, thresholds and acceptance criteria were fixed on 2026-11-10, before the first execution. Transfers are coplanar two-impulse LEO (6 678 km) to GEO (42 164 km); Hohmann: 3 892.608 m/s, 18 990.05 s. Budget 10^3 D evaluations as in the Phase 3 benchmark. Success: a feasible solution within 1 m/s of the reference whose plan reaches the target and whose constraints still hold when recomputed from a numerical propagation (tolerance 1e-6 of each scale). Scenario 'time-limited': duration at most 0.8 of the Hohmann time, so the limit binds; reference from problems.references. 'tight-budget': delta-v budget of 1.02 times Hohmann, which does not bind at the optimum but leaves a thin feasible region. 'altitude-floor': minimum altitude equal to the altitude of the initial orbit (299 863 m), so every transfer that first descends is infeasible and the optimum lies on the constraint. 'propellant-short': 2 000 kg on board where the cheapest transfer needs 2 132 kg, so no feasible transfer exists and the only correct outcome is to report none. Penalty coefficients are in m/s and multiply the sum of squared normalized violations: 1e4 makes a 1 % violation cost 1 m/s, the success threshold; 1e8 makes a 0.01 % violation cost 1 m/s.

constraint_handling.rationale: weak penalty: a 1 % normalized violation costs 1 m/s, the success threshold of the benchmark
strong penalty: a 0.01 % normalized violation costs 1 m/s; four orders above the weak one to expose the sensitivity to the coefficient
